story_angle: solemn obituary for a beloved institution nobody can remember the purpose of
headline: Federal Caravan Relay Standards Board Drives Off Into the Sunset
deck: Quietly dissolved amidst complaints about neon permits while Congress examines Ottoman motels as the future of long-distance travel.
article:
The Federal Caravan Relay Standards Board, once tasked with cross-country oversight, has been dissolved following years of handling disputes over lantern fuel and neon signage for motels. Founded after the 1956 caravan mandates, it shifted to logging grievances about motel sign brightness.

Its final directive referenced outdated mileage tables requiring 400 miles daily. Outgoing Commissioner Reginald P. Whetstone noted the indifference to their efforts. As Congress considers Ottoman relay inns amid Gulf Caravan issues, the board's end highlights how some agencies simply cease without fanfare.
author: Eleanor Planville, Chief Bureaucratic Correspondent

oped.title: Neon Permits Saved Us From Hatless Anarchy
oped.author: Lord Percival Glowforge, Emeritus Chair of Unnecessary Illumination at the Society for Prolonged Journeys
oped.body: The dissolution of the Federal Caravan Relay Standards Board is nothing short of national betrayal. Those neon permit rules existed for good reason: without them, every relay station would descend into visual chaos, and my own modest chain of seventeen glow-lit outposts would lose its competitive edge over those dreary Ottoman dynasties Congress now favors. Complainants whine about bureaucracy, yet they never mention their own garish hat collections that blinded oncoming caravans for miles. The true fix is obvious—mandate uniform crimson fezzes for all travelers and outlaw private signage entirely. My stations would then become the sole legal beacons, naturally. America remains vast; only disciplined neon can shrink it back to manageable weeks. Blaming the board ignores how hatless ingrates caused every delay.

classifieds.text: For Sale: 47 unused neon permit kits and a stack of obsolete relay flags from the late Federal Caravan Relay Standards Board. Owner must liquidate before Congress seizes everything for the Ottoman Motel pilot program.
Help Wanted: Ottoman Motel Syndicate needs a night manager who can handle six-week guest stays and field calls from angry congressmen about the dissolved relay board. Room and beans included.
Public Notice: Any traveler still holding a valid 2025 neon permit may exchange it for a complimentary week at the new Congressional Ottoman Rest Plaza before the paperwork expires in 2028.

Personals: Apologetic husband seeks forgiving wife to resume our stalled Nebraska-to-Nevada honeymoon now that the relay board is gone. Will supply extra spare tires and no more arguments about neon stickers.

panels.caption: "The Relay Board dissolved over neon permit delays," the aide muttered, watching the chairman's caravan pull away.
A senator leaned in: "Standards are dead. Congress is funding the Ottoman Motel chain—they already own every water stop."
"Perfect," the aide said. "My grandkids can inherit the bill."

joke.setup: The Federal Caravan Relay Standards Board announced its dissolution this week after 38 years of enforcing axle-width rules no one could enforce west of the Mississippi.
joke.punchline: Their closing statement is still crossing Kansas on a mule train and should reach the capital sometime after the next election cycle.

sponsor_ads.headline: Board’s Sunset Means Our Relay Starts at Dawn
sponsor_ads.body: With federal standards evaporating like last week’s radiator fluid, the McSorley Dynasty now offers unregulated three-week handoffs between our Nebraska and Nevada properties. No inspectors, no forms, just the same faded lobby carpet your grandparents memorized.
sponsor_ads.tagline: Rates unchanged since the Eisenhower administration; everything else has.

sponsor_ads.headline: Drive Off With Us Instead
sponsor_ads.body: The Federal Caravan Relay Standards Board may have left the building, but our mule-train escort service still honors every obsolete guideline they ever printed. Book the full Omaha-to-Tucson circuit before the roads decide they miss regulation.
sponsor_ads.tagline: Arrive when we say or inherit a motel key.

sponsor_ads.headline: America’s Too Big for One Board
sponsor_ads.body: Now that the regulators have driven into legend, the Intergenerational Motel Trust invites you to spend the next fiscal quarter rotating between our fourteen properties along the former Route 66 alignment. Complimentary continental breakfast every morning for the next 26 days.
sponsor_ads.tagline: Checkout is optional; the highway never was.

sponsor_ads.headline: Final Regulated Caravan—Batteries Not Included
sponsor_ads.body: The last convoy operating under the late board’s rules departs tomorrow; after that you’re on your own with whatever fuel dynasty still remembers your grandfather’s credit. We sell the maps that used to be classified.

stories.headline: Dynasty Motel Holdings Posts Record Occupancy After Board Dissolution
stories.deck: Neon permit backlog forces chains to lease Ottoman-style annexes from county historical societies
stories.article:
Shares in multi-state motel families climbed after the Federal Caravan Relay Standards Board ended operations, leaving thousands of permit requests for additional neon signage unresolved. Operators along Route 66 now lease surplus rooms from shuttered divorce courts to handle overflow caravans waiting on updated rest regulations.

Analysts attribute the gains to Congress floating Ottoman relay inn designs as replacements for standard lobbies, though local tax assessors continue billing properties under the 1947 two-lane commercial code.

stories.headline: Midwest Grain Co-ops Extend Silo Leases at Highway Junction Motels
stories.deck: Harvest crews schedule deliveries around established caravan turnaround times at state-line rest stops
stories.article:
Iowa corn cooperatives have renewed annual leases on motel parking lots to store overflow grain while caravans complete multi-day hauls to Gulf terminals. The arrangement follows the dissolution of relay standards that once set uniform loading intervals for agricultural freight.

Extension agents now recommend planting schedules aligned with the three-week average trip duration from Des Moines to Houston, reducing spoilage claims filed under the old Eisenhower-era warehouse statutes.

real_world_echo: US and Iran trade more strikes in Gulf mirrored as third-week Gulf Caravan Raids prompting the Board's quiet dissolution, with Congress pivoting to Ottoman relay inns instead
